chicken-caesar-wraps.html.storage: Store the cooked chicken, dressing and washed, dried lettuce in separate covered containers in the fridge; keep croutons dry in an airtight container. Use the chilled ingredients within 48 hours of cooking the chicken. Assemble just before eating.
chicken-caesar-wraps.html.freezing: Freeze cooled cooked chicken in labelled portions for up to 2 months for best quality. Tortillas can be frozen separately if the packet allows. Make the dressing and lettuce fresh and add croutons at the end; finished wraps become soggy.
chicken-caesar-wraps.html.reheating: Serve the chicken cold after safe chilling, or reheat it once in a covered pan with a splash of water until steaming hot throughout. Heat the tortilla separately and add the lettuce, dressing and croutons afterwards.
chicken-caesar-wraps.html.substitutions: Little gem lettuce works instead of romaine. Replace croutons with small pieces of toasted bread. Use extra mayonnaise in place of yoghurt for a richer dressing. If avoiding fish, choose an anchovy-free alternative to Worcestershire sauce and check its label.

steak-ciabatta.html.storage: Keep the steak and onions in separate covered containers in the fridge and use within 48 hours of cooking. Store the Dijon mayonnaise and rocket separately; toast and fill the bread just before eating.
steak-ciabatta.html.freezing: Freeze cooled steak and onions in separate labelled portions for up to 2 months for best quality. Freeze ciabatta separately if suitable. Add fresh rocket and mayonnaise after defrosting; steak may be less tender after freezing.
steak-ciabatta.html.reheating: Cold sliced steak works well in a freshly toasted roll. If reheating, heat the steak and onions once in a covered pan with a splash of water until steaming hot throughout; the steak will cook beyond medium-rare. Add rocket and mayonnaise afterwards.
steak-ciabatta.html.substitutions: Use a baguette or sourdough instead of ciabatta. Rump and sirloin both work; slice across the grain. Swap rocket for watercress or baby spinach, and use wholegrain mustard if you prefer a milder texture.

mozzarella-pesto-toasties.html.storage: Best eaten straight from the pan. If saving leftovers, cool and refrigerate in a covered container within 2 hours and eat within 48 hours. For preparation ahead, keep drained mozzarella and tomato separate from the bread until ready to toast.
mozzarella-pesto-toasties.html.freezing: The tomato and fresh mozzarella can release water after freezing, so freeze spare bread on its own and make the filling fresh. Freezing the finished toastie is not recommended for the best texture.
mozzarella-pesto-toasties.html.reheating: Reheat once in an oven at 180°C / 160°C fan until the filling is steaming hot throughout, turning if needed. Cover loosely with foil if the bread browns before the middle heats through. Microwaving will soften the crust.
mozzarella-pesto-toasties.html.substitutions: Use cheddar or a mozzarella-cheddar mix for a stronger, less watery filling. Roasted peppers, drained well, can replace tomato. For a vegetarian version, use pesto made with vegetarian cheese; check the label for nuts and other allergens if relevant.

coronation-chicken-sandwiches.html.storage: Keep the chicken filling in a covered container in the fridge and use within 48 hours of cooking the chicken. Store lettuce separately and assemble just before eating; made-up sandwiches are best the same day.
coronation-chicken-sandwiches.html.freezing: Freeze the cooled cooked chicken before adding the dressing, in labelled portions, for up to 2 months for best quality. Freeze bread separately. The mayonnaise and yoghurt dressing may split, and lettuce loses its crunch, so make those fresh.
coronation-chicken-sandwiches.html.reheating: This filling is best served cold. After defrosting plain cooked chicken in the fridge, mix with freshly made dressing and eat within 24 hours. Do not warm the dressed sandwich.
coronation-chicken-sandwiches.html.substitutions: Use plain yoghurt instead of Greek yoghurt, or replace the yoghurt with extra mayonnaise for a richer dressing. Apricot chutney can replace mango chutney. Try rolls or wraps in place of sliced bread.

chicken-shawarma-flatbreads.html.storage: Keep cooked chicken, garlic yoghurt and salad in separate covered containers in the fridge. Use within 48 hours of cooking the chicken. Fill the flatbreads just before eating so they stay soft rather than soggy.
chicken-shawarma-flatbreads.html.freezing: Freeze cooled cooked chicken in labelled portions for up to 2 months for best quality, and freeze flatbreads separately if their packet allows. Make the salad and garlic yoghurt fresh; they do not retain their texture well after freezing.
chicken-shawarma-flatbreads.html.reheating: Reheat the chicken in a covered frying pan with a splash of water, turning until steaming hot throughout. Warm the bread separately and add cold sauce and salad after heating. Only reheat the chicken once.
chicken-shawarma-flatbreads.html.substitutions: Use pitta breads or tortilla wraps instead of flatbreads. Plain yoghurt works for the marinade and sauce. Swap the salad vegetables for shredded cabbage and grated carrot. Keep chicken breast as the meat.

crispy-halloumi-pittas.html.storage: For the best texture, cook the halloumi just before eating. Keep any cooked halloumi, slaw and yoghurt sauce in separate covered containers in the fridge and use within 48 hours. Fill pittas at the last moment.
crispy-halloumi-pittas.html.freezing: The assembled pittas are best made fresh: the vegetables soften and the yoghurt sauce may separate after freezing. Freeze spare pitta breads separately, following the packet instructions.
crispy-halloumi-pittas.html.reheating: Reheat cooked halloumi once in a dry non-stick pan over a medium heat, turning until steaming hot throughout. It may be firmer than when freshly fried. Warm the pitta separately, then add the cold slaw and sauce.
crispy-halloumi-pittas.html.substitutions: Use wraps or flatbreads instead of pittas. White cabbage works in place of red cabbage. Swap the sweet chilli sauce for a little honey and chilli flakes to taste; choose vegetarian-labelled cheese if needed.

greek-chicken-couscous-salad.html.storage: Cool the chicken and couscous promptly in separate shallow containers, then refrigerate. Keep the cucumber, tomato, feta and dressing separate where possible and use everything within 48 hours of cooking. Assemble when ready to eat.
greek-chicken-couscous-salad.html.freezing: Freeze cooled cooked chicken and plain couscous in separate labelled portions for up to 2 months for best quality. Add fresh cucumber, tomato, herbs, feta and dressing after defrosting; the finished salad is best not frozen.
greek-chicken-couscous-salad.html.reheating: The chilled salad can be eaten cold. For a warm version, reheat only the chicken and plain couscous until steaming hot throughout, adding a splash of water and stirring the couscous. Add the cold salad ingredients afterwards. Reheat only once.
greek-chicken-couscous-salad.html.substitutions: Use cooked quinoa instead of couscous, following its packet for liquid and cooking time; cool it promptly. Swap feta for a similar salad cheese, or leave out the olives and add extra tomatoes. For a meat-free version, use drained chickpeas instead of chicken.

croque-monsieur.html.storage: Cool leftover sandwiches and refrigerate in a covered container within 2 hours; eat within 48 hours. For a fresher result, make the white sauce ahead, chill it separately, and assemble the sandwiches just before baking. Follow the ham packet’s shorter storage limit if given.
croque-monsieur.html.freezing: For the best texture, freeze the bread separately and assemble with fresh filling and sauce. The white sauce can separate and the bread can soften after freezing, so the finished sandwich is best made fresh.
croque-monsieur.html.reheating: Reheat a chilled sandwich once in an oven at 180°C / 160°C fan until the centre is steaming hot throughout. Cover loosely with foil if the cheese browns too quickly. The middle takes longer than the top, so check before serving.
croque-monsieur.html.substitutions: Use Emmental or mature cheddar instead of Gruyère. Semi-skimmed milk also works in the sauce. Replace ham with cooked, well-drained mushrooms for a meat-free version, and choose vegetarian-labelled cheese. Leave out the nutmeg if you prefer.

korean-style-gochujang-beef-pork-bibimba.storage: Cool rice as quickly as possible, ideally within 1 hour, and refrigerate in shallow portions. Eat the rice, and any leftovers mixed with it, within 24 hours. Keep other cooked components separate and use within 48 hours. For microwave rice, follow the packet; once heated, do not heat it again.
korean-style-gochujang-beef-pork-bibimba.freezing: Freeze suitable cooled components separately for up to 2 months for best quality. If freezing freshly cooked rice, cool it quickly and freeze within 1 hour. Defrost in the fridge and use within 24 hours. Use freshly cooked rice for portions intended for reheating; do not refreeze or save already reheated rice for another hot meal.
korean-style-gochujang-beef-pork-bibimba.reheating: Reheat rice only once until steaming hot throughout and eat immediately. Heat other cooked components thoroughly, keeping cold toppings separate. The recipe uses microwave rice: if that rice has already been heated, make fresh rice instead of reheating it again. Reheat the mince separately.
korean-style-gochujang-beef-pork-bibimba.substitutions: Use all-beef mince instead of the beef-and-pork mix. Broccoli can replace green beans. Gochujang brands vary, so add gradually rather than replacing it spoon-for-spoon with a much hotter chilli paste.

indonesian-chicken-poke-bowl.html.storage: Cool rice as quickly as possible, ideally within 1 hour, and refrigerate in shallow portions. Eat the rice, and any leftovers mixed with it, within 24 hours. Keep other cooked components separate and use within 48 hours. Store cabbage, edamame and sauce separately for a fresher texture.
indonesian-chicken-poke-bowl.html.freezing: Freeze suitable cooled components separately for up to 2 months for best quality. If freezing freshly cooked rice, cool it quickly and freeze within 1 hour. Defrost in the fridge and use within 24 hours. Do not freeze the dressed cabbage. Microwave rice that has already been heated should not be saved for reheating again.
indonesian-chicken-poke-bowl.html.reheating: Reheat rice only once until steaming hot throughout and eat immediately. Heat other cooked components thoroughly, keeping cold toppings separate. Make fresh rice if the microwave rice has already been heated once. Reheat the chicken and sweet potato separately before adding the chilled toppings.
indonesian-chicken-poke-bowl.html.substitutions: Swap sweet potato for squash, allowing for its cooking time. Use peas instead of edamame, cooking them as directed. Reduce the sambal for less heat and keep chicken breast as the meat.

moroccan-meatball-bowl.html.storage: Cool rice as quickly as possible, ideally within 1 hour, and refrigerate in shallow portions. Eat the rice, and any leftovers mixed with it, within 24 hours. Keep other cooked components separate and use within 48 hours. Keep yoghurt and chopped salad separate from the meatballs and rice.
moroccan-meatball-bowl.html.freezing: Freeze suitable cooled components separately for up to 2 months for best quality. If freezing freshly cooked rice, cool it quickly and freeze within 1 hour. Defrost in the fridge and use within 24 hours. Freeze meatballs in their tomato sauce; add yoghurt and chopped salad fresh.
moroccan-meatball-bowl.html.reheating: Reheat rice only once until steaming hot throughout and eat immediately. Heat other cooked components thoroughly, keeping cold toppings separate. Check the middle of the meatballs is steaming hot; add yoghurt and fresh vegetables after heating.
moroccan-meatball-bowl.html.substitutions: Use beef mince or lamb mince in the meatballs. Panko works instead of fresh breadcrumbs if needed; moisten it first. Cook any alternative rice using its own packet ratio and timing.

thai-curry-bowl.html.storage: Cool rice as quickly as possible, ideally within 1 hour, and refrigerate in shallow portions. Eat the rice, and any leftovers mixed with it, within 24 hours. Keep other cooked components separate and use within 48 hours. Keep the thick curry and rice separate; add crunchy toppings at serving.
thai-curry-bowl.html.freezing: Freeze suitable cooled components separately for up to 2 months for best quality. If freezing freshly cooked rice, cool it quickly and freeze within 1 hour. Defrost in the fridge and use within 24 hours. The coconut sauce may separate slightly; stir it back together as it heats.
thai-curry-bowl.html.reheating: Reheat rice only once until steaming hot throughout and eat immediately. Heat other cooked components thoroughly, keeping cold toppings separate. Warm the curry gently in a saucepan, stirring to recombine the coconut milk.
thai-curry-bowl.html.substitutions: Use firm tofu instead of chicken breast, and soy sauce instead of fish sauce if preferred. Curry pastes vary in strength and may contain shrimp; check the label and add gradually.

truffle pasta.html.storage: Cool promptly, refrigerate covered within 2 hours and eat within 48 hours. Label the container with the recipe name and the date and time it was made; follow any shorter ingredient use-by or opened-pack instructions.
truffle pasta.html.freezing: Freezing not recommended for the finished crème fraîche pasta. Make fresh for the best sauce and pasta texture.
truffle pasta.html.reheating: Reheat once in a pan with a splash of water, stirring until steaming hot throughout. Add fresh herbs or cheese after heating. Keep the heat gentle so the creamy sauce does not catch.
truffle pasta.html.substitutions: Use crème fraîche rather than cream for the original tangy sauce. Chestnut mushrooms work well; swap tenderstem for small broccoli florets and cook until tender.

harissa-prawn-orzo.html.storage: Cool promptly, refrigerate covered within 2 hours and eat within 48 hours. If the prawns were already cooked before being added, eat the dish freshly made rather than planning another reheating. Label the container with the recipe name and the date and time it was made; follow any shorter ingredient use-by or opened-pack instructions.
harissa-prawn-orzo.html.freezing: Freezing not recommended for this finished prawn dish. Make only the portions you need and follow the chilled leftover instructions.
harissa-prawn-orzo.html.reheating: If the prawns were raw when added and cooked in this recipe, reheat a chilled portion only once, adding a splash of water and stirring until the orzo and the centres of the prawns are steaming hot throughout. If ready-cooked prawns were heated in the recipe, do not reheat the leftovers again; eat safely chilled leftovers cold within the storage limit. If unsure of the prawns' previous heating history, do not reheat.
harissa-prawn-orzo.html.substitutions: Use small broccoli florets instead of green beans. Harissa varies in heat, so start with less. If using ready-cooked prawns, add only at the end to heat through and do not reheat them again.

pastina.html.storage: Cool promptly, refrigerate covered within 2 hours and eat within 48 hours. Label the container with the recipe name and the date and time it was made; follow any shorter ingredient use-by or opened-pack instructions.
pastina.html.freezing: Freezing not recommended for the finished pastina, especially when made with cream. The small pasta absorbs liquid; make fresh for the best texture.
pastina.html.reheating: Reheat once in a pan with a splash of water, stirring until steaming hot throughout. Add fresh herbs or cheese after heating. Add milk or stock little by little to bring back the creamy texture.
pastina.html.substitutions: Use another tiny soup pasta and follow its packet cooking time. Milk gives a lighter finish than cream. Use vegetarian hard cheese and vegetable stock for a vegetarian version.

baked-ziti.html.storage: Cool in shallow portions and refrigerate covered within 2 hours. Eat within 48 hours.
baked-ziti.html.freezing: Freeze cooled individual portions, tightly wrapped, for up to 2 months for best quality. Defrost fully in the fridge. Keep a little extra tomato sauce with each portion to prevent dryness.
baked-ziti.html.reheating: Reheat once in an oven at 180°C / 160°C fan until steaming hot in the centre. Cover if the top browns before the middle is hot; portion size affects the time.
baked-ziti.html.substitutions: Use penne or rigatoni instead of ziti. All-beef mince can replace the beef-and-sausage mixture. Cottage cheese can replace ricotta, but drain it if very wet.

carbonara.html.storage: Cool promptly, refrigerate covered within 2 hours and eat within 48 hours.
carbonara.html.freezing: Freeze cooled portions for up to 2 months for best quality. Pasta softens after freezing; freezing the sauce separately gives a better result. For a silky egg sauce, making carbonara fresh is preferable; freezing makes it grainier.
carbonara.html.reheating: Reheat once in a pan with a splash of water, stirring until steaming hot throughout. Add fresh herbs or cheese after heating. The egg sauce may set as it heats; prioritise heating it fully rather than preserving the original silky texture.
carbonara.html.substitutions: Use guanciale or pancetta; smoked bacon gives a different but workable flavour. All-Parmesan can replace the mixed cheeses. It will taste milder than a sauce made with pecorino.

mediterranean-pasta-salad.html.storage: Refrigerate covered and eat within 48 hours of cooking any pasta or chicken. Keep the dressing and watery vegetables separate where possible; add leafy greens just before eating.
mediterranean-pasta-salad.html.freezing: The assembled salad is best not frozen: cucumber, tomatoes and leaves lose their texture. Freeze suitable cooked meat or plain pasta separately if preparing ahead.
mediterranean-pasta-salad.html.reheating: Serve cold after safe chilling. If you want warm cooked components, reheat those once until steaming hot throughout before adding fresh salad and dressing.
mediterranean-pasta-salad.html.substitutions: Use any short pasta. Replace feta with mozzarella, or add drained chickpeas instead of the optional chicken. Use lemon juice instead of balsamic for a sharper dressing.

pesto-pasta-salad.html.storage: Refrigerate covered and eat within 48 hours of cooking any pasta or chicken. Keep the dressing and watery vegetables separate where possible; add leafy greens just before eating.
pesto-pasta-salad.html.freezing: The assembled salad is best not frozen: cucumber, tomatoes and leaves lose their texture. Freeze suitable cooked meat or plain pasta separately if preparing ahead.
pesto-pasta-salad.html.reheating: Serve cold after safe chilling. If you want warm cooked components, reheat those once until steaming hot throughout before adding fresh salad and dressing.
pesto-pasta-salad.html.substitutions: Use green or red pesto to taste, and mozzarella or feta. For a vegetarian version choose pesto and cheese labelled vegetarian. Check the pesto ingredients if avoiding nuts.

jalfrezi.html.storage: Cool promptly and refrigerate covered within 2 hours. Use within 48 hours, or sooner if the base gravy has an earlier storage limit.
jalfrezi.html.freezing: Freeze portions for later reheating only when made with freshly cooked chicken and freshly made gravy in this cooking session. Otherwise freeze the gravy separately before finishing the curry. Defrost fully in the fridge and use within 24 hours.
jalfrezi.html.reheating: Reheat once until steaming hot throughout. If chilled chicken or gravy was already reheated when making this curry, do not reheat the finished curry again.
jalfrezi.html.substitutions: For a milder curry, halve the fresh chillies and chilli powder. Use ordinary tomato purée diluted as listed, not four tablespoons of concentrated purée.

pathia.html.storage: Cool promptly and refrigerate covered within 2 hours. Use within 48 hours, or sooner if the base gravy has an earlier storage limit.
pathia.html.freezing: Freeze portions for later reheating only when made with freshly cooked chicken and freshly made gravy in this cooking session. Otherwise freeze the gravy separately before finishing the curry. Defrost fully in the fridge and use within 24 hours.
pathia.html.reheating: Reheat once until steaming hot throughout. If chilled chicken or gravy was already reheated when making this curry, do not reheat the finished curry again.
pathia.html.substitutions: If using tamarind concentrate, start with ½ tsp for 2 servings instead of the 2 tsp sauce and taste before adding more. Omit optional Worcestershire for a fish-free version; standard Worcestershire contains anchovies.

moghul.html.storage: Cool promptly and refrigerate covered within 2 hours. Use within 48 hours, or sooner if the base gravy has an earlier storage limit.
moghul.html.freezing: Freeze portions for later reheating only when made with freshly cooked chicken and freshly made gravy in this cooking session. Otherwise freeze the gravy separately before finishing the curry. Defrost fully in the fridge and use within 24 hours.
moghul.html.reheating: Reheat once until steaming hot throughout. If chilled chicken or gravy was already reheated when making this curry, do not reheat the finished curry again.
moghul.html.substitutions: Contains almonds and dairy. Omit optional Worcestershire for a fish-free version; standard Worcestershire contains anchovies. Optional sultanas, ghee and egg stay out of the shopping list unless selected.

basegravy.html.storage: Cool in shallow containers, refrigerate covered within 2 hours and eat within 48 hours.
basegravy.html.freezing: Freeze cooled portions in sealed, labelled containers for up to 2 months for best quality. Leave expansion space. Freeze in recipe-sized portions so you can thaw only what you need.
basegravy.html.reheating: Reheat once in a saucepan, stirring and adding a splash of water or stock, until steaming hot throughout. Only heat the portion needed for the curry; do not repeatedly warm the whole batch.
basegravy.html.substitutions: Use brown onions if Spanish onions are unavailable. Keep the stock-free vegetable base mild so individual curries can be seasoned separately. Blend thoroughly for a smooth gravy.

slow-cooker-beef-rendang.html.storage: Divide into shallow containers to cool, refrigerate within 2 hours and eat within 48 hours.
slow-cooker-beef-rendang.html.freezing: Freeze cooled portions with their sauce for up to 2 months for best quality. Label before freezing. Keep the toasted coconut mixed into the sauce; coconut milk may separate slightly.
slow-cooker-beef-rendang.html.reheating: Reheat once on the hob or in the microwave until steaming hot throughout; stir and turn meat pieces so the centre heats evenly. Do not use the slow cooker to reheat chilled leftovers. Stir gently to avoid breaking the tender beef; add water sparingly to keep the thick sauce.
slow-cooker-beef-rendang.html.substitutions: Use beef chuck or braising steak as written; lean quick-fry steak dries out during long cooking. Lemon zest changes the flavour but can replace unavailable lime leaves; remove whole spices before serving.

slow-cooker-tuscan-chicken.html.storage: Divide into shallow containers to cool, refrigerate within 2 hours and eat within 48 hours. Label the container with the recipe name and the date and time it was made; follow any shorter ingredient use-by or opened-pack instructions.
slow-cooker-tuscan-chicken.html.freezing: Freezing not recommended for the finished dish with cream, Parmesan and spinach. Make fresh for the best sauce texture.
slow-cooker-tuscan-chicken.html.reheating: Reheat once on the hob or in the microwave until steaming hot throughout; stir and turn meat pieces so the centre heats evenly. Do not use the slow cooker to reheat chilled leftovers. Use gentle heat and stir the sauce; avoid a rolling boil that can split the cream.
slow-cooker-tuscan-chicken.html.substitutions: Keep chicken breast as the meat. Use kale instead of spinach, adding it earlier so it softens. Crème fraîche can replace cream, giving a tangier finish.

slow-cooker-chicken-chorizo-butter-bean-.storage: Divide into shallow containers to cool, refrigerate within 2 hours and eat within 48 hours.
slow-cooker-chicken-chorizo-butter-bean-.freezing: Freeze cooled portions with their sauce for up to 2 months for best quality. Label before freezing. Freeze the beans in the sauce; they may become a little softer.
slow-cooker-chicken-chorizo-butter-bean-.reheating: Reheat once on the hob or in the microwave until steaming hot throughout; stir and turn meat pieces so the centre heats evenly. Do not use the slow cooker to reheat chilled leftovers. Stir carefully so the beans and chicken stay in pieces.
slow-cooker-chicken-chorizo-butter-bean-.substitutions: Keep chicken breast as the meat. Cannellini beans can replace butter beans. Use roasted fresh peppers instead of jarred peppers, and adjust salt to match the chorizo.

slow-cooker-smoky-hot-chilli-con-carne.h.storage: Divide into shallow containers to cool, refrigerate within 2 hours and eat within 48 hours.
slow-cooker-smoky-hot-chilli-con-carne.h.freezing: Freeze cooled portions with their sauce for up to 2 months for best quality. Label before freezing. Freeze before adding any yoghurt, cheese or other fresh toppings.
slow-cooker-smoky-hot-chilli-con-carne.h.reheating: Reheat once on the hob or in the microwave until steaming hot throughout; stir and turn meat pieces so the centre heats evenly. Do not use the slow cooker to reheat chilled leftovers. Add a splash of water if the thick sauce catches; serve with freshly prepared toppings.
slow-cooker-smoky-hot-chilli-con-carne.h.substitutions: Use black beans instead of kidney beans. For a milder chilli, reduce the fresh chillies, hot chilli powder and chipotle; extra chocolate does not remove heat.

ginger-lime-chicken-noodle-soup.html.storage: Cool in shallow containers, refrigerate covered within 2 hours and eat within 48 hours. Noodles absorb broth, so keep them separate when preparing ahead.
ginger-lime-chicken-noodle-soup.html.freezing: Freeze cooled portions in sealed, labelled containers for up to 2 months for best quality. Leave expansion space. Freeze the chicken broth without noodles and spinach for a better texture; add those fresh.
ginger-lime-chicken-noodle-soup.html.reheating: Reheat once in a saucepan, stirring and adding a splash of water or stock, until steaming hot throughout. Make sure chicken pieces are hot in the centre, then add freshly cooked noodles and spinach.
ginger-lime-chicken-noodle-soup.html.substitutions: Use chicken breast as written. Pak choi can replace spinach; add its stems before the leaves. Rice noodles work instead of udon, but cook them according to their own packet.

satay-beef-noodles.html.storage: Cool promptly in shallow portions, refrigerate covered within 2 hours and eat within 48 hours.
satay-beef-noodles.html.freezing: Freeze cooled portions for up to 2 months for best quality, but noodles and vegetables will soften. Keep fresh garnishes separate. Keep peanuts and lime wedges fresh for serving.
satay-beef-noodles.html.reheating: Reheat once in a frying pan, adding water a tablespoon at a time and tossing until steaming hot throughout. In the microwave, stir halfway and check the centre is steaming hot. The noodles absorb sauce as they stand, so loosen the peanut sauce again just before serving.
satay-beef-noodles.html.substitutions: Use pork mince instead of beef, or browned firm tofu for a meat-free version. Tahini changes the flavour but can replace peanut butter; it contains sesame and is not an allergen-free swap.

sticky-gochujang-chicken-noodles.html.storage: Cool promptly in shallow portions, refrigerate covered within 2 hours and eat within 48 hours.
sticky-gochujang-chicken-noodles.html.freezing: Freeze cooled portions for up to 2 months for best quality, but noodles and vegetables will soften. Keep fresh garnishes separate. Add sesame seeds, lime juice and spring onion garnish after reheating.
sticky-gochujang-chicken-noodles.html.reheating: Reheat once in a frying pan with a splash of water, tossing until steaming hot throughout. In the microwave, stir or turn halfway and check the centre is hot. Use enough water to loosen the sticky glaze without turning it into soup.
sticky-gochujang-chicken-noodles.html.substitutions: Use chicken breast as written. Thinly sliced cabbage can replace pak choi; add it before tender leaves. Egg noodles can replace udon if cooked to their packet instructions.

chicken-chow-mein.html.storage: Cool promptly in shallow portions, refrigerate covered within 2 hours and eat within 48 hours. Cook beansprouts as directed before storing the finished dish.
chicken-chow-mein.html.freezing: Freeze cooled portions for up to 2 months for best quality, but noodles and vegetables will soften. Keep fresh garnishes separate. Beansprouts will soften; for best crunch, add freshly cooked beansprouts when finishing.
chicken-chow-mein.html.reheating: Reheat once in a frying pan with a splash of water, tossing until steaming hot throughout. In the microwave, stir or turn halfway and check the centre is hot. Toss in batches so the chicken and noodles heat evenly, not just the outside of the pan.
chicken-chow-mein.html.substitutions: Use chicken breast as written. Tenderstem broccoli can replace some cabbage; cut it small. Mushroom stir-fry sauce can replace oyster sauce, though the flavour and saltiness differ.

coconutty-caribbean-soup.html.storage: Cool in shallow containers, refrigerate covered within 2 hours and eat within 48 hours.
coconutty-caribbean-soup.html.freezing: Freeze cooled portions in sealed, labelled containers for up to 2 months for best quality. Leave expansion space. Stir to recombine the coconut milk after thawing.
coconutty-caribbean-soup.html.reheating: Reheat once in a saucepan, stirring and adding a splash of water or stock, until steaming hot throughout. Keep the sweet potato pieces intact by stirring gently.
coconutty-caribbean-soup.html.substitutions: Use squash instead of sweet potato, roasting until tender. Kidney beans can replace black beans. Jerk seasoning varies in salt and heat; start with less and adjust.

minestrone.html.storage: Cool in shallow containers, refrigerate covered within 2 hours and eat within 48 hours.
minestrone.html.freezing: Freeze cooled portions in sealed, labelled containers for up to 2 months for best quality. Leave expansion space. For better texture freeze the soup before adding pasta and greens, then add them fresh.
minestrone.html.reheating: Reheat once in a saucepan, stirring and adding a splash of water or stock, until steaming hot throughout. The pasta absorbs stock, so add extra liquid as needed.
minestrone.html.substitutions: Use seasonal vegetables and small pasta shapes. Omit pancetta and choose vegetarian stock and cheese for a vegetarian version; add extra beans for body.

carrot-coriander-soup.html.storage: Cool in shallow containers, refrigerate covered within 2 hours and eat within 48 hours.
carrot-coriander-soup.html.freezing: Freeze cooled portions in sealed, labelled containers for up to 2 months for best quality. Leave expansion space.
carrot-coriander-soup.html.reheating: Reheat once in a saucepan, stirring and adding a splash of water or stock, until steaming hot throughout.
carrot-coriander-soup.html.substitutions: Use vegetable stock for a vegetarian soup. Replace potato with a little extra carrot for a lighter result; blend well. Add fresh coriander after reheating for a brighter flavour.

roasted-red-pepper-soup.html.storage: Cool in shallow containers, refrigerate covered within 2 hours and eat within 48 hours.
roasted-red-pepper-soup.html.freezing: Freeze cooled portions in sealed, labelled containers for up to 2 months for best quality. Leave expansion space. Freeze without any fresh garnish.
roasted-red-pepper-soup.html.reheating: Reheat once in a saucepan, stirring and adding a splash of water or stock, until steaming hot throughout. Add water or stock if the tomato-rich soup becomes too thick.
roasted-red-pepper-soup.html.substitutions: Drained jarred roasted peppers can replace freshly roasted peppers; reduce any added salt. Use olive oil instead of butter for a dairy-free version, checking the stock label.

broccoli-stilton-soup.html.storage: Cool in shallow containers, refrigerate covered within 2 hours and eat within 48 hours.
broccoli-stilton-soup.html.freezing: Freeze cooled portions in sealed, labelled containers for up to 2 months for best quality. Leave expansion space. The cheese may separate slightly; blend briefly after reheating if needed.
broccoli-stilton-soup.html.reheating: Reheat once in a saucepan, stirring and adding a splash of water or stock, until steaming hot throughout. Warm gently and stir well rather than boiling hard.
broccoli-stilton-soup.html.substitutions: Use another blue cheese instead of Stilton, or mature cheddar for a milder soup. Vegetable stock makes it meat-free; choose vegetarian-labelled cheese if required.

pea-asparagus-soup.html.storage: Cool in shallow containers, refrigerate covered within 2 hours and eat within 48 hours. Label the container with the recipe name and the date and time it was made; follow any shorter ingredient use-by or opened-pack instructions.
pea-asparagus-soup.html.freezing: Freezing not recommended once the cream has been added. For batch cooking, freeze the cooled soup base without cream for up to 2 months for best quality; defrost in the fridge and use within 24 hours. Reheat once until steaming hot and add fresh cream when serving.
pea-asparagus-soup.html.reheating: Reheat once in a saucepan, stirring and adding a splash of water or stock, until steaming hot throughout. Add fresh chives at the end.
pea-asparagus-soup.html.substitutions: Use vegetable stock instead of chicken stock. Swap asparagus for tender broccoli, cooking until soft before blending. Oat cream can replace double cream, with a different flavour.

spiced-carrot-lentil-soup.html.storage: Cool in shallow containers, refrigerate covered within 2 hours and eat within 48 hours.
spiced-carrot-lentil-soup.html.freezing: Freeze cooled portions in sealed, labelled containers for up to 2 months for best quality. Leave expansion space. The lentils thicken on standing, so allow room to add liquid later.
spiced-carrot-lentil-soup.html.reheating: Reheat once in a saucepan, stirring and adding a splash of water or stock, until steaming hot throughout. Stir frequently so the thick lentil soup does not stick.
spiced-carrot-lentil-soup.html.substitutions: Use an unsweetened plant drink instead of milk for a dairy-free version, checking the stock. Add chilli gradually. Keep split red lentils; whole green lentils need different cooking and give a different texture.

french-onion-soup.html.storage: Cool in shallow containers, refrigerate covered within 2 hours and eat within 48 hours. Keep baguette and cheese separate from the soup until serving.
french-onion-soup.html.freezing: Freeze cooled portions in sealed, labelled containers for up to 2 months for best quality. Leave expansion space. Freeze the onion soup without the bread and cheese topping.
french-onion-soup.html.reheating: Reheat once in a saucepan, stirring and adding a splash of water or stock, until steaming hot throughout. Heat the soup fully first, then add fresh toast and cheese and grill until melted.
french-onion-soup.html.substitutions: Use Emmental or mature cheddar instead of Gruyère. Replace wine with extra stock and a little lemon juice to taste. Vegetable stock and vegetarian cheese give a meat-free variation.

spiced-parsnip-soup.html.storage: Cool in shallow containers, refrigerate covered within 2 hours and eat within 48 hours. Label the container with the recipe name and the date and time it was made; follow any shorter ingredient use-by or opened-pack instructions.
spiced-parsnip-soup.html.freezing: Freezing not recommended after the cream garnish has been added. The cooled soup base without cream or chilli oil can be frozen for up to 2 months for best quality; defrost in the fridge and use within 24 hours. Reheat once until steaming hot, then add fresh garnishes.
spiced-parsnip-soup.html.reheating: Reheat once in a saucepan, stirring and adding a splash of water or stock, until steaming hot throughout. Add the cream swirl and chilli oil just before eating.
spiced-parsnip-soup.html.substitutions: Use ground cumin and coriander if garam masala is unavailable, adjusting to taste. Omit the cream or use an unsweetened plant cream; check stock for a dairy-free version.

leek-and-potato-soup.html.storage: Cool in shallow containers, refrigerate covered within 2 hours and eat within 48 hours. Label the container with the recipe name and the date and time it was made; follow any shorter ingredient use-by or opened-pack instructions.
leek-and-potato-soup.html.freezing: Freezing not recommended once cream or crème fraîche has been added. The cooled soup base without dairy can be frozen for up to 2 months for best quality; defrost in the fridge and use within 24 hours. Reheat once until steaming hot, then add fresh dairy and heat through gently.
leek-and-potato-soup.html.reheating: Reheat once in a saucepan, stirring and adding a splash of water or stock, until steaming hot throughout. Stir in the cream after heating the soup, then heat through gently.
leek-and-potato-soup.html.substitutions: Use double cream or crème fraîche as written; the latter adds tang. Use unsweetened plant cream for a dairy-free variation and check the stock.

sofritto-ragu.html.storage: Cool promptly and refrigerate in a clean covered container within 2 hours. Use within 48 hours; this homemade sauce is not shelf-stable.
sofritto-ragu.html.freezing: Freeze cooled sauce in small labelled portions for up to 2 months for best quality. Leave room for expansion. Freeze in portions sized for pasta or lasagne.
sofritto-ragu.html.reheating: Reheat only the amount needed, once, in a saucepan, stirring until steaming hot throughout. Add a little water if too thick. Turn and break up the meat as it heats so no cold pockets remain.
sofritto-ragu.html.substitutions: Use all-beef mince in place of the beef-and-pork mixture. Stock can replace red wine. Omitting pancetta gives a less smoky, less salty sauce; season at the end.

vinaigrette.html.storage: Keep in a clean sealed jar in the fridge and use within 48 hours. Olive oil can turn cloudy or firm when chilled; shake before using. This dressing is not a shelf-stable preserve.
vinaigrette.html.freezing: Best mixed fresh rather than frozen; freezing can separate the dressing and dull its flavour.
vinaigrette.html.reheating: No reheating needed. Let only the portion you need loosen briefly at room temperature, then shake or whisk and use straight away.
vinaigrette.html.substitutions: Use lemon juice or a wine vinegar as written. Maple syrup can replace honey. Wholegrain mustard gives a grainier dressing; adjust the acidity and sweetness to taste.

jack-daniels-sauce.html.storage: Cool promptly and refrigerate in a clean covered container within 2 hours. Use within 48 hours; this homemade sauce is not shelf-stable.
jack-daniels-sauce.html.freezing: Freeze cooled sauce in small labelled portions for up to 2 months for best quality. Leave room for expansion. The pineapple pieces will soften but remain suitable for a glaze.
jack-daniels-sauce.html.reheating: Reheat only the amount needed, once, in a saucepan, stirring until steaming hot throughout. Add a little water if too thick. Stir often because the sugary glaze catches easily.
jack-daniels-sauce.html.substitutions: Replace whiskey with extra pineapple juice for an alcohol-free variation, and check the other sauces. Simmer to the desired consistency; do not assume brief cooking removes all alcohol.

panda-express-orange-chicken-sauce.html.storage: Cool promptly and refrigerate in a clean covered container within 2 hours. Use within 48 hours; this homemade sauce is not shelf-stable.
panda-express-orange-chicken-sauce.html.freezing: Freeze cooled sauce in small labelled portions for up to 2 months for best quality. Leave room for expansion. The cornflour-thickened sauce can loosen after thawing; stir it well.
panda-express-orange-chicken-sauce.html.reheating: Reheat only the amount needed, once, in a saucepan, stirring until steaming hot throughout. Add a little water if too thick. If still too thin after heating, simmer briefly while stirring.
panda-express-orange-chicken-sauce.html.substitutions: Use tamari instead of soy sauce if needed, checking labels. Fresh orange juice works; add chilli gradually. The cornflour is the thickener, so do not swap it spoon-for-spoon with ordinary flour.

nacho-cheese-sauce.html.storage: Cool quickly and refrigerate covered within 2 hours. Use within 48 hours and follow any shorter milk storage instructions.
nacho-cheese-sauce.html.freezing: Best made fresh. Freezing can make the cheese sauce grainy; if preparing ahead, refrigerate rather than freezing.
nacho-cheese-sauce.html.reheating: Reheat once over a low heat, whisking in a splash of milk until smooth and steaming hot throughout. Do not boil vigorously or the cheese may split.
nacho-cheese-sauce.html.substitutions: Use mature cheddar for a stronger flavour or processed American cheese for a smoother sauce. Reduce cayenne for less heat. Ordinary unsweetened milk works; plant milks will change the texture.

lemon-chicken-salad.html.storage: Refrigerate covered and eat within 48 hours of cooking any pasta or chicken. Keep the dressing and watery vegetables separate where possible; add leafy greens just before eating. Avocado browns quickly, so cut it just before eating.
lemon-chicken-salad.html.freezing: The assembled salad is best not frozen: cucumber, tomatoes and leaves lose their texture. Freeze suitable cooked meat or plain pasta separately if preparing ahead.
lemon-chicken-salad.html.reheating: Serve cold after safe chilling. If you want warm cooked components, reheat those once until steaming hot throughout before adding fresh salad and dressing.
lemon-chicken-salad.html.substitutions: Use little gem or mixed leaves. Replace optional avocado with extra cucumber, or use drained chickpeas instead of chicken. Add nuts only if suitable for everyone eating.

acai-bowl.html.storage: Best blended and eaten straight away. Refrigerate any untopped leftovers promptly in a covered container and use within 24 hours; the colour and texture will change. Keep granola and toppings separate.
acai-bowl.html.freezing: Freeze the untopped blended base promptly in small sealed portions for up to 1 month for best texture. Thaw in the fridge just enough to blend again, and use within 24 hours of thawing. Check the frozen-fruit packet for any handling instructions.
acai-bowl.html.reheating: Do not heat the finished bowl. If frozen berries require cooking on their packet, cook them first and chill safely before blending. Add fresh banana and crunchy toppings when serving.
acai-bowl.html.substitutions: Keep açaí powder and a normal ripe banana as written. Use your usual milk or unsweetened plant drink, and adjust gradually. Swap berries to taste; choose toppings that suit any allergies.

cottage-pie.html.storage: Cool in shallow portions and refrigerate covered within 2 hours. Eat within 48 hours.
cottage-pie.html.freezing: Freeze cooled individual portions, tightly wrapped, for up to 2 months for best quality. Defrost fully in the fridge. Freeze individual portions or a shallow dish; potato texture may soften slightly.
cottage-pie.html.reheating: Reheat once in an oven at 180°C / 160°C fan until steaming hot in the centre. Cover if the top browns before the middle is hot; portion size affects the time.
cottage-pie.html.substitutions: Use lamb mince for a shepherd’s-pie variation. Stock can replace wine. Add extra carrot or peas if liked; keep the filling thick so the mash sits on top.

creamy-garlic-chicken.html.storage: Divide into shallow containers to cool, refrigerate within 2 hours and eat within 48 hours. Label the container with the recipe name and the date and time it was made; follow any shorter ingredient use-by or opened-pack instructions.
creamy-garlic-chicken.html.freezing: Freezing not recommended for the finished cream sauce and chicken. Make fresh for the best sauce texture and follow the chilled leftover instructions.
creamy-garlic-chicken.html.reheating: Reheat once on the hob or in the microwave until steaming hot throughout; stir and turn meat pieces so the centre heats evenly. Do not use the slow cooker to reheat chilled leftovers. Heat the chicken through gently in the sauce and avoid prolonged boiling.
creamy-garlic-chicken.html.substitutions: Use chicken breast as written. Replace wine with extra chicken stock and a little lemon juice to taste. Crème fraîche gives a tangier sauce than double cream.

smash-cheeseburgers.html.storage: Best freshly cooked. Cool leftovers, refrigerate covered within 2 hours and use within 48 hours. Keep sauce and cold garnishes separate where possible. Store cooked patties separately from buns, pickles and burger sauce.
smash-cheeseburgers.html.freezing: Wrap cooled cooked patties individually and freeze in a sealed container for up to 2 months for best quality. Freeze buns separately. Add fresh burger sauce, pickles and any salad after reheating; do not freeze assembled burgers for the best texture.
smash-cheeseburgers.html.reheating: Reheat the meat once on a tray in an oven at 180°C / 160°C fan until steaming hot throughout. Turn as needed; add sauce only at the end. Microwaving softens the coating. Reheat patties fully before building a fresh burger; toast buns separately.
smash-cheeseburgers.html.substitutions: Use the beef mince as written for the smash texture. Swap burger cheese for thin cheddar slices. Lettuce or sliced tomato can be added fresh; avoid mixing vegetables into the mince.

lemon-garlic-oregano-chicken-traybake.ht.storage: Cool in shallow portions and refrigerate covered within 2 hours. Eat within 48 hours.
lemon-garlic-oregano-chicken-traybake.ht.freezing: Freeze cooled individual portions, tightly wrapped, for up to 2 months for best quality. Defrost fully in the fridge. Potatoes lose some crispness; freeze with the chicken juices to reduce dryness.
lemon-garlic-oregano-chicken-traybake.ht.reheating: Reheat once in an oven at 180°C / 160°C fan until steaming hot in the centre. Cover if the top browns before the middle is hot; portion size affects the time. Add a splash of water and cover the chicken while heating; uncover potatoes at the end if desired.
lemon-garlic-oregano-chicken-traybake.ht.substitutions: Use chicken breast as written. Swap red onion for brown onion. Small potato chunks need a head start so the breast does not overcook.

broccoli-quiche.html.storage: Cool in shallow portions and refrigerate covered within 2 hours. Eat within 48 hours. Label the container with the recipe name and the date and time it was made; follow any shorter ingredient use-by or opened-pack instructions.
broccoli-quiche.html.freezing: Freezing not recommended for this finished recipe, particularly when made with cream. Make fresh for the best filling and pastry texture.
broccoli-quiche.html.reheating: Reheat once in an oven at 180°C / 160°C fan until steaming hot in the centre. Cover if the top browns before the middle is hot; portion size affects the time. Heat until the egg filling is hot in the centre; protect pastry edges if they brown first.
broccoli-quiche.html.substitutions: Use well-drained spinach or cooked leeks instead of broccoli. Gruyère can replace cheddar. Keep the egg-and-milk balance; a smaller tin may be needed when reducing servings.

lemon-cheesecake.html.storage: Keep covered in the fridge at 0–5°C and eat within 48 hours of making. Refrigerate promptly after cooling and return leftovers to the fridge straight after serving; follow any shorter dairy use-by date. Label the container with the recipe name and the date and time it was made; follow any shorter ingredient use-by or opened-pack instructions.
lemon-cheesecake.html.freezing: Freezing not recommended for the finished cheesecake with its soured cream and fresh toppings. Keep chilled and make fresh for serving.
lemon-cheesecake.html.reheating: Serve chilled. Do not reheat the finished dessert.
lemon-cheesecake.html.substitutions: Use digestive or plain oat biscuits for the base. Keep full-fat soft cheese and mascarpone for the intended set. Lime can replace lemon, added to taste rather than assuming the same number of fruit.

chocolate-chip-cookies.html.storage: Store cooled cookies in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For best texture, eat within 3 days. Do not seal while warm or the trapped steam will soften them.
chocolate-chip-cookies.html.freezing: Freeze cooled cookies, separated with parchment, for up to 2 months for best quality. Thaw only the number wanted in their covered container. Raw dough portions can also be frozen if tightly wrapped; bake through before eating.
chocolate-chip-cookies.html.reheating: Eat at room temperature, or warm baked cookies briefly in a low oven until the chocolate softens. They can dry out quickly; no need to make them piping hot like a meat dish.
chocolate-chip-cookies.html.substitutions: Use chopped chocolate instead of chips. Keep the flour, butter and sugar balance for the same spread; a different sugar mix changes chewiness. Do not eat raw dough containing flour or egg.

caramel-fudge.html.storage: Once set, keep covered in the fridge and eat within 48 hours, following any shorter storage instructions on the added caramel. The fridge makes the fudge firmer; take out only the portion you are about to eat. Label the container with the recipe name and the date and time it was made; follow any shorter ingredient use-by or opened-pack instructions.
caramel-fudge.html.freezing: Freezing not recommended for this finished cream fudge recipe. Keep the set fudge chilled and make the quantity you need.
caramel-fudge.html.reheating: No reheating needed. Let a small serving soften briefly before eating. Re-melting the finished fudge can spoil its set and texture.
caramel-fudge.html.substitutions: Use golden syrup instead of glucose syrup if necessary, expecting a slightly different flavour and set. Vanilla extract can replace paste in a smaller amount to taste. Follow the sugar temperature in the method.

carrot-cake.html.storage: Keep covered in the fridge at 0–5°C and eat within 48 hours of making. Refrigerate promptly after cooling and return leftovers to the fridge straight after serving; follow any shorter dairy use-by date.
carrot-cake.html.freezing: Freeze cooled uniced cake layers, well wrapped, for up to 2 months for best quality. Defrost in the fridge and add freshly made icing; use within 24 hours of defrosting. The soft-cheese icing is best made fresh.
carrot-cake.html.reheating: Serve chilled. Do not reheat the finished dessert. Take out only the slice you want shortly before eating so it loses its fridge chill; keep the rest refrigerated.
carrot-cake.html.substitutions: Leave out optional walnuts if preferred and check all labels if avoiding nuts. Sultanas can replace raisins. Keep full-fat soft cheese for a firmer icing; changing tin size changes baking time.

creme-brulee.html.storage: Keep covered in the fridge at 0–5°C and eat within 48 hours of making. Refrigerate promptly after cooling and return leftovers to the fridge straight after serving; follow any shorter dairy use-by date. Add the caramelised sugar only just before serving so it stays crisp. Label the container with the recipe name and the date and time it was made; follow any shorter ingredient use-by or opened-pack instructions.
creme-brulee.html.freezing: Freezing not recommended for the finished cream custard. Keep chilled and caramelise the sugar just before serving.
creme-brulee.html.reheating: Serve chilled. Do not reheat the finished dessert. Caramelising fresh sugar on the chilled custard is the finishing step, not reheating the custard underneath.
creme-brulee.html.substitutions: Vanilla extract can replace the pod; add to taste. Keep the cream and egg-yolk quantities for the intended custard set. A dairy-free version needs a different tested recipe.

key-lime-pie.html.storage: Keep covered in the fridge at 0–5°C and eat within 48 hours of making. Refrigerate promptly after cooling and return leftovers to the fridge straight after serving; follow any shorter dairy use-by date. Label the container with the recipe name and the date and time it was made; follow any shorter ingredient use-by or opened-pack instructions.
key-lime-pie.html.freezing: Freezing not recommended for the finished pie with whipped cream. Keep chilled and add fresh cream just before serving.
key-lime-pie.html.reheating: Serve chilled. Do not reheat the finished dessert.
key-lime-pie.html.substitutions: Use digestive biscuits instead of oatmeal biscuits if preferred. Ordinary limes work; lemon gives a different pie. Use full-fat condensed milk as written, not evaporated milk.

harissa-salmon-crispy-potatoes.html.storage: Cool in shallow portions and refrigerate covered within 2 hours. Eat within 48 hours. Keep yoghurt sauce separate and eat leftovers within 24 hours for best quality.
harissa-salmon-crispy-potatoes.html.freezing: Freeze cooled individual portions, tightly wrapped, for up to 2 months for best quality. Defrost fully in the fridge. Freeze cooled fish and potatoes separately from the yoghurt sauce; fish becomes firmer and potatoes less crisp.
harissa-salmon-crispy-potatoes.html.reheating: Reheat once in an oven at 180°C / 160°C fan until steaming hot in the centre. Cover if the top browns before the middle is hot; portion size affects the time. Check the salmon is hot in the centre, not just warm on the surface; add cold yoghurt sauce afterwards.
harissa-salmon-crispy-potatoes.html.substitutions: Use the salmon fillets as written; adjust cooking for their thickness. Reduce harissa for less heat. Plain yoghurt works instead of Greek yoghurt but makes a looser sauce.

sofritto-ragu-lasagne.html.storage: Cool in shallow portions and refrigerate covered within 2 hours. Eat within 48 hours.
sofritto-ragu-lasagne.html.freezing: Freeze cooled individual portions, tightly wrapped, for up to 2 months for best quality. Defrost fully in the fridge. Freeze in individual portions with enough sauce to keep the pasta moist.
sofritto-ragu-lasagne.html.reheating: Reheat once in an oven at 180°C / 160°C fan until steaming hot in the centre. Cover if the top browns before the middle is hot; portion size affects the time.
sofritto-ragu-lasagne.html.substitutions: Use stock instead of red wine. All-beef mince can replace the beef-and-pork mixture. Choose lasagne sheets that suit the method and follow any packet pre-cooking instructions.

sofritto-ragu-tagliatelle.html.storage: Cool promptly, refrigerate covered within 2 hours and eat within 48 hours.
sofritto-ragu-tagliatelle.html.freezing: Freeze cooled portions for up to 2 months for best quality. Pasta softens after freezing; freezing the sauce separately gives a better result. Freeze the ragù separately and cook fresh pasta when serving for the best result.
sofritto-ragu-tagliatelle.html.reheating: Reheat once in a pan with a splash of water, stirring until steaming hot throughout. Add fresh herbs or cheese after heating.
sofritto-ragu-tagliatelle.html.substitutions: Use pappardelle or another broad pasta instead of tagliatelle. Stock can replace wine, and all-beef mince can replace the mixed mince.

jack-daniels-glazed-chicken.html.storage: Best freshly cooked. Cool leftovers, refrigerate covered within 2 hours and use within 48 hours. Keep sauce and cold garnishes separate where possible. Keep coleslaw chilled separately; do not warm it with the chicken.
jack-daniels-glazed-chicken.html.freezing: Freeze cooled cooked chicken, glaze and potato wedges separately in labelled containers for up to 2 months for best quality. Make or buy fresh coleslaw when serving. The wedges will be less crisp after thawing.
jack-daniels-glazed-chicken.html.reheating: Reheat the meat once on a tray in an oven at 180°C / 160°C fan until steaming hot throughout. Turn as needed; add sauce only at the end. Microwaving softens the coating. The sugary glaze can burn: heat chicken fully first, then brush with heated glaze at the end.
jack-daniels-glazed-chicken.html.substitutions: Keep chicken breast as the meat. Replace whiskey with pineapple juice for an alcohol-free glaze and check the teriyaki sauce. Use sweet potato wedges instead of ordinary potatoes, adjusting cooking time.

panda-express-orange-chicken.html.storage: Cool rice as quickly as possible, ideally within 1 hour, and refrigerate in shallow portions. Eat the rice, and any leftovers mixed with it, within 24 hours. Keep other cooked components separate and use within 48 hours. Keep crispy chicken, orange sauce, broccoli and rice separate for better texture. If rice was already reheated, do not heat it again.
panda-express-orange-chicken.html.freezing: Freeze suitable cooled components separately for up to 2 months for best quality. If freezing freshly cooked rice, cool it quickly and freeze within 1 hour. Defrost in the fridge and use within 24 hours. The chicken coating softens after freezing; freeze sauce separately. Use freshly cooked rice for portions intended for freezing and reheating.
panda-express-orange-chicken.html.reheating: Reheat rice only once until steaming hot throughout and eat immediately. Heat other cooked components thoroughly, keeping cold toppings separate. Heat chicken once on an oven tray until steaming hot, then coat with reheated sauce. If the supplied cooked rice has already been reheated, make fresh rice.
panda-express-orange-chicken.html.substitutions: Keep chicken breast as written. Use tenderstem broccoli or small florets. Tamari can replace soy sauce if suitable, checking labels and saltiness.

chicken-stroganoff.html.storage: Cool rice as quickly as possible, ideally within 1 hour, and refrigerate in shallow portions. Eat the rice, and any leftovers mixed with it, within 24 hours. Keep other cooked components separate and use within 48 hours. Keep rice separate from the stroganoff. Label the container with the recipe name and the date and time it was made; follow any shorter ingredient use-by or opened-pack instructions.
chicken-stroganoff.html.freezing: Freezing not recommended for the finished crème fraîche stroganoff. Keep any rice separate and follow the shorter rice storage limit.
chicken-stroganoff.html.reheating: Reheat rice only once until steaming hot throughout and eat immediately. Heat other cooked components thoroughly, keeping cold toppings separate. Heat the chicken sauce gently and stir; avoid vigorous boiling that can split the dairy.
chicken-stroganoff.html.substitutions: Use chicken breast as written. Soured cream gives a tangier, less heat-stable sauce than crème fraîche; stir it in gently. Chestnut mushrooms work instead of white mushrooms.

focaccia.html.storage: Let the loaf cool completely, then store wrapped in a clean bread bag or bread bin in a cool, dry place. Eat within 2 days for best texture; refrigeration makes plain bread stale faster. Discard the whole loaf if mould appears.
focaccia.html.freezing: Slice cooled bread, wrap well and freeze for up to 2 months for best quality. Separate slices so you can take out only what you need. Thaw covered at room temperature, or toast individual slices from frozen.
focaccia.html.reheating: Toast slices, or refresh a loaf briefly in an oven at 180°C / 160°C fan. Heat only what you need so repeated warming does not dry it out.
focaccia.html.substitutions: Use rosemary as written, or thyme. Add drained olives or roasted garlic before baking, keeping wet toppings modest. Strong bread flour gives the intended structure.

tiger-bread.html.storage: Let the loaf cool completely, then store wrapped in a clean bread bag or bread bin in a cool, dry place. Eat within 2 days for best texture; refrigeration makes plain bread stale faster. Discard the whole loaf if mould appears.
tiger-bread.html.freezing: Slice cooled bread, wrap well and freeze for up to 2 months for best quality. Separate slices so you can take out only what you need. Thaw covered at room temperature, or toast individual slices from frozen.
tiger-bread.html.reheating: Toast slices, or refresh a loaf briefly in an oven at 180°C / 160°C fan. Heat only what you need so repeated warming does not dry it out.
tiger-bread.html.substitutions: Keep rice flour in the topping for its characteristic crackle; wheat flour gives a different crust. Neutral oil can replace sesame oil, with a milder flavour.

sourdough.html.storage: Let the loaf cool completely, then store wrapped in a clean bread bag or bread bin in a cool, dry place. Eat within 2 days for best texture; refrigeration makes plain bread stale faster. Discard the whole loaf if mould appears.
sourdough.html.freezing: Slice cooled bread, wrap well and freeze for up to 2 months for best quality. Separate slices so you can take out only what you need. Thaw covered at room temperature, or toast individual slices from frozen.
sourdough.html.reheating: Toast slices, or refresh a loaf briefly in an oven at 180°C / 160°C fan. Heat only what you need so repeated warming does not dry it out.
sourdough.html.substitutions: Use strong white bread flour as written for the intended hydration. Wholemeal absorbs more water and changes proving, so substitute only a small part initially. Keep starter maintenance separate from loaf scaling.

jambalaya.html.storage: Cool rice as quickly as possible, ideally within 1 hour, and refrigerate in shallow portions. Eat the rice, and any leftovers mixed with it, within 24 hours. Keep other cooked components separate and use within 48 hours. Because the rice is mixed into the dish, the whole jambalaya has the 24-hour fridge limit.
jambalaya.html.freezing: Divide freshly cooked jambalaya into shallow single portions, cool quickly and freeze within 1 hour of cooking. Label and use within 2 months for best quality. Defrost fully in the fridge and use within 24 hours; do not freeze a portion that has already been reheated.
jambalaya.html.reheating: Reheat rice only once until steaming hot throughout and eat immediately. Heat other cooked components thoroughly, keeping cold toppings separate. Stir several times and check both the rice and chicken centres; add a splash of stock if dry.
jambalaya.html.substitutions: Use chicken breast and chorizo as written. Use smoked paprika and extra chicken instead of chorizo for a different, less rich version. Keep long-grain rice unless adjusting liquid and cooking to another variety.

slow-cooker-beef-bourguignon.html.storage: Divide into shallow containers to cool, refrigerate within 2 hours and eat within 48 hours.
slow-cooker-beef-bourguignon.html.freezing: Freeze cooled portions with their sauce for up to 2 months for best quality. Label before freezing. Mushrooms and onions may soften but the sauce freezes well.
slow-cooker-beef-bourguignon.html.reheating: Reheat once on the hob or in the microwave until steaming hot throughout; stir and turn meat pieces so the centre heats evenly. Do not use the slow cooker to reheat chilled leftovers. Turn larger pieces of beef and check they are hot all the way through.
slow-cooker-beef-bourguignon.html.substitutions: Use braising or stewing beef, not quick-fry steak. Beef stock can replace wine, giving a different flavour. Chestnut mushrooms work instead of closed-cup mushrooms.

slow-cooker-chicken-chasseur.html.storage: Divide into shallow containers to cool, refrigerate within 2 hours and eat within 48 hours.
slow-cooker-chicken-chasseur.html.freezing: Freeze cooled portions with their sauce for up to 2 months for best quality. Label before freezing. Freeze before the butter finish if preparing ahead; stir in butter after reheating.
slow-cooker-chicken-chasseur.html.reheating: Reheat once on the hob or in the microwave until steaming hot throughout; stir and turn meat pieces so the centre heats evenly. Do not use the slow cooker to reheat chilled leftovers. Reheat gently in the sauce so the breast stays as moist as possible.
slow-cooker-chicken-chasseur.html.substitutions: Keep chicken breast as the meat. Use a sliced onion instead of banana shallots. Chicken stock can replace red wine; add a little lemon juice at the end to taste.

penne-arrabbiata.html.storage: Cool promptly, refrigerate covered within 2 hours and eat within 48 hours.
penne-arrabbiata.html.freezing: Freeze cooled portions for up to 2 months for best quality. Pasta softens after freezing; freezing the sauce separately gives a better result. The tomato sauce freezes particularly well on its own.
penne-arrabbiata.html.reheating: Reheat once in a pan with a splash of water, stirring until steaming hot throughout. Add fresh herbs or cheese after heating.
penne-arrabbiata.html.substitutions: Use rigatoni or another short pasta. Chopped tomatoes can replace plum tomatoes; reduce to the same thick consistency. Adjust chilli gradually, especially with a different brand.

meatball-penne.html.storage: Cool promptly, refrigerate covered within 2 hours and eat within 48 hours.
meatball-penne.html.freezing: Freeze cooled portions for up to 2 months for best quality. Pasta softens after freezing; freezing the sauce separately gives a better result. Freeze meatballs in their sauce and cook fresh penne for a better texture.
meatball-penne.html.reheating: Reheat once in a pan with a splash of water, stirring until steaming hot throughout. Add fresh herbs or cheese after heating. Turn meatballs as they heat and check their centres are steaming hot.
meatball-penne.html.substitutions: Use all-beef mince instead of the beef-and-pork mixture. Use another short pasta shape. Choose vegetarian hard cheese if making a separate meat-free version with a suitable meatball substitute.

thai-chicken-curry.html.storage: Cool rice as quickly as possible, ideally within 1 hour, and refrigerate in shallow portions. Eat the rice, and any leftovers mixed with it, within 24 hours. Keep other cooked components separate and use within 48 hours. Keep the curry and rice separate.
thai-chicken-curry.html.freezing: Freeze suitable cooled components separately for up to 2 months for best quality. If freezing freshly cooked rice, cool it quickly and freeze within 1 hour. Defrost in the fridge and use within 24 hours. Coconut milk may separate slightly; stir it together as the curry heats.
thai-chicken-curry.html.reheating: Reheat rice only once until steaming hot throughout and eat immediately. Heat other cooked components thoroughly, keeping cold toppings separate. Warm the curry gently while checking the chicken is hot in the centre.
thai-chicken-curry.html.substitutions: Keep chicken breast and Mae Ploy green or red paste as written. Reduce paste for less heat rather than adding extra sugar. Tofu and vegetarian curry paste make a different meat-free variation; many pastes contain shrimp.

chicken-leek-mushroom-pie.html.storage: Cool in shallow portions and refrigerate covered within 2 hours. Eat within 48 hours. Label the container with the recipe name and the date and time it was made; follow any shorter ingredient use-by or opened-pack instructions.
chicken-leek-mushroom-pie.html.freezing: Freezing not recommended for this finished cream-filled pie. Make fresh for the best sauce and pastry texture.
chicken-leek-mushroom-pie.html.reheating: Reheat once in an oven at 180°C / 160°C fan until steaming hot in the centre. Cover if the top browns before the middle is hot; portion size affects the time. The filling takes longer to heat than the pastry; cover the lid with foil if needed.
chicken-leek-mushroom-pie.html.substitutions: Keep chicken breast as written. Chestnut or white mushrooms both work. Shortcrust can replace puff pastry, but follow its baking instructions and check the filling is fully hot.

moroccan-chicken-filo-pie.html.storage: Cool in shallow portions and refrigerate covered within 2 hours. Eat within 48 hours.
moroccan-chicken-filo-pie.html.freezing: Freeze cooled individual portions, tightly wrapped, for up to 2 months for best quality. Defrost fully in the fridge. Freeze the cooled filling separately and add fresh filo after thawing for a crisper top.
moroccan-chicken-filo-pie.html.reheating: Reheat once in an oven at 180°C / 160°C fan until steaming hot in the centre. Cover if the top browns before the middle is hot; portion size affects the time. Protect the filo with loose foil if it colours before the chicken filling is hot.
moroccan-chicken-filo-pie.html.substitutions: Keep chicken breast as written. Omit the almonds if preferred; check the other ingredients if avoiding nuts. Puff pastry is an alternative topping with a different texture and baking time.

chicken-chorizo-potato-bake.html.storage: Cool in shallow portions and refrigerate covered within 2 hours. Eat within 48 hours.
chicken-chorizo-potato-bake.html.freezing: Freeze cooled individual portions, tightly wrapped, for up to 2 months for best quality. Defrost fully in the fridge. Potato slices will be softer after thawing.
chicken-chorizo-potato-bake.html.reheating: Reheat once in an oven at 180°C / 160°C fan until steaming hot in the centre. Cover if the top browns before the middle is hot; portion size affects the time. Check the chicken and sauce under the potato layer, not only the golden top.
chicken-chorizo-potato-bake.html.substitutions: Keep chicken breast as written. Swap red pepper for yellow pepper. For a chorizo-free variation use extra chicken breast and a little more smoked paprika, adjusting salt.

greek-beef-pastitsio.html.storage: Cool in shallow portions and refrigerate covered within 2 hours. Eat within 48 hours.
greek-beef-pastitsio.html.freezing: Freeze cooled individual portions, tightly wrapped, for up to 2 months for best quality. Defrost fully in the fridge. Cool and slice into portions before wrapping for easier thawing.
greek-beef-pastitsio.html.reheating: Reheat once in an oven at 180°C / 160°C fan until steaming hot in the centre. Cover if the top browns before the middle is hot; portion size affects the time. The dense pasta layers need time to heat in the middle; cover the top if needed.
greek-beef-pastitsio.html.substitutions: Use rigatoni or penne as written. Beef stock can replace red wine. Lamb mince gives a different but suitable variation; cook it fully before layering.

spinach-ricotta-cannelloni.html.storage: Cool in shallow portions and refrigerate covered within 2 hours. Eat within 48 hours.
spinach-ricotta-cannelloni.html.freezing: Freeze cooled individual portions, tightly wrapped, for up to 2 months for best quality. Defrost fully in the fridge. Keep the tubes well covered with sauce so they do not dry out.
spinach-ricotta-cannelloni.html.reheating: Reheat once in an oven at 180°C / 160°C fan until steaming hot in the centre. Cover if the top browns before the middle is hot; portion size affects the time. Check the ricotta filling in the centre tubes is hot, not just the sauce around the edge.
spinach-ricotta-cannelloni.html.substitutions: Use frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed very dry, in place of fresh; judge the amount by the drained cooked spinach. Choose vegetarian-labelled hard cheese if needed.

sausage-leek-mustard-gratin.html.storage: Cool in shallow portions and refrigerate covered within 2 hours. Eat within 48 hours. Label the container with the recipe name and the date and time it was made; follow any shorter ingredient use-by or opened-pack instructions.
sausage-leek-mustard-gratin.html.freezing: Freezing not recommended for this finished cream gratin. Make fresh for the best sauce and potato texture.
sausage-leek-mustard-gratin.html.reheating: Reheat once in an oven at 180°C / 160°C fan until steaming hot in the centre. Cover if the top browns before the middle is hot; portion size affects the time. Check a sausage piece and the sauce beneath the potatoes are steaming hot.
sausage-leek-mustard-gratin.html.substitutions: Use your preferred pork sausages, checking their cooking instructions. Mature cheddar can replace other hard cheese. Dijon gives a smoother sauce than wholegrain mustard.

aubergine-parmigiana.html.storage: Cool in shallow portions and refrigerate covered within 2 hours. Eat within 48 hours.
aubergine-parmigiana.html.freezing: Freeze cooled individual portions, tightly wrapped, for up to 2 months for best quality. Defrost fully in the fridge. The aubergine layers soften slightly after thawing; wrap portions well.
aubergine-parmigiana.html.reheating: Reheat once in an oven at 180°C / 160°C fan until steaming hot in the centre. Cover if the top browns before the middle is hot; portion size affects the time. Rest briefly after heating so the layers hold when served.
aubergine-parmigiana.html.substitutions: Use vegetarian-labelled hard cheese for a vegetarian dish. Well-drained mozzarella helps the layers hold together. Roasted courgette gives a different, wetter variation; drain well before layering.

crispy-chilli-beef.html.storage: Cool rice as quickly as possible, ideally within 1 hour, and refrigerate in shallow portions. Eat the rice, and any leftovers mixed with it, within 24 hours. Keep other cooked components separate and use within 48 hours. Keep beef, sauce and rice separate where possible; the coating softens once sauced.
crispy-chilli-beef.html.freezing: Freeze suitable cooled components separately for up to 2 months for best quality. If freezing freshly cooked rice, cool it quickly and freeze within 1 hour. Defrost in the fridge and use within 24 hours. Freeze cooked beef and sauce separately; the coating will be less crisp after thawing.
crispy-chilli-beef.html.reheating: Reheat rice only once until steaming hot throughout and eat immediately. Heat other cooked components thoroughly, keeping cold toppings separate. Reheat the beef once on an oven tray until steaming hot, then toss with reheated sauce; heat rice separately.
crispy-chilli-beef.html.substitutions: Use sirloin or rump sliced thinly across the grain. Reduce fresh chilli and use a mild sweet chilli sauce for less heat. Rice vinegar can be replaced with a little cider vinegar to taste.

salt-pepper-chicken.html.storage: Best freshly cooked. Cool leftovers, refrigerate covered within 2 hours and use within 48 hours. Keep sauce and cold garnishes separate where possible.
salt-pepper-chicken.html.freezing: Freeze cooled cooked meat separately from sauce and salad for up to 2 months for best quality. The coating will be less crisp after thawing. Keep the vegetable garnish separate; it loses crunch after freezing.
salt-pepper-chicken.html.reheating: Reheat the meat once on a tray in an oven at 180°C / 160°C fan until steaming hot throughout. Turn as needed; add sauce only at the end. Microwaving softens the coating. Add freshly stir-fried vegetables after reheating for better crunch.
salt-pepper-chicken.html.substitutions: Keep chicken breast as written. Yellow or green pepper can replace red pepper. Reduce chilli and white pepper for a milder finish; add seasoning in stages rather than all at once.

shakshuka.html.storage: For making ahead, refrigerate the tomato-pepper sauce without eggs within 2 hours and use within 48 hours. Cook eggs fresh at serving. If storing the finished dish, fully cook the eggs, chill promptly and use within 24 hours for best quality.
shakshuka.html.freezing: Freeze the cooled sauce without eggs in labelled portions for up to 2 months for best quality. Defrost in the fridge and add fresh eggs when finishing.
shakshuka.html.reheating: Reheat sauce once until steaming hot, then cook fresh eggs in it. The finished eggs become firm and rubbery on reheating, so making only the number needed gives a better result.
shakshuka.html.substitutions: Add drained chickpeas to the sauce for extra substance. Use yellow peppers instead of red. Reduce chilli for less heat, and add fresh parsley after cooking.

fluffy-pancakes.html.storage: Cool plain pancakes on a rack, then refrigerate covered within 2 hours. Eat within 48 hours. Keep berries and maple syrup separate until serving.
fluffy-pancakes.html.freezing: Freeze cooled pancakes separated with parchment in a sealed bag for up to 2 months for best quality. Defrost in the fridge before reheating; keep fruit toppings fresh.
fluffy-pancakes.html.reheating: Reheat once in a low oven, loosely covered, or in a dry pan, turning until hot throughout. A microwave works but gives a softer surface.
fluffy-pancakes.html.substitutions: Use your usual milk or an unsweetened plant drink. A little plain yoghurt alongside the fruit makes a tangier topping. Wholemeal flour changes fluffiness, so substitute only part at first.

breakfast-wraps.html.storage: Cool the cooked filling promptly and refrigerate within 2 hours; eat within 48 hours. Keep tomato separate where possible to avoid soggy tortillas. Make only as many wraps as you intend to eat hot.
breakfast-wraps.html.freezing: Freeze cooled wraps without tomato, tightly wrapped individually, for up to 1 month for best texture. Defrost in the fridge; the scrambled egg may be firmer after freezing.
breakfast-wraps.html.reheating: Reheat once, loosely covered in an oven at 180°C / 160°C fan, until the egg and bacon filling is steaming hot in the centre. Uncover briefly to crisp the tortilla.
breakfast-wraps.html.substitutions: Use mushrooms instead of bacon for a meat-free version, frying off their moisture first. Swap cheddar for another melting cheese. Use small pieces of drained roasted pepper instead of tomato.

brioche-french-toast.html.storage: Cool cooked French toast on a rack and refrigerate covered within 2 hours. Eat within 48 hours. Keep maple butter separate in the fridge; do not store bread soaking in leftover raw egg mixture. Label the container with the recipe name and the date and time it was made; follow any shorter ingredient use-by or opened-pack instructions.
brioche-french-toast.html.freezing: Freezing not recommended for this finished cream-and-egg French toast recipe. Cook fresh for the best texture; never store bread soaking in leftover raw egg mixture.
brioche-french-toast.html.reheating: Reheat once on a tray in an oven at 180°C / 160°C fan until the egg-soaked centre is hot throughout. Turn if needed; a pan can colour the outside before the middle is hot.
brioche-french-toast.html.substitutions: Use thick sliced challah or soft white bread instead of brioche. Milk can replace cream for a less rich version. Keep the egg mixture set through the bread, whatever loaf you use.

amatriciana.html.storage: Cool promptly, refrigerate covered within 2 hours and eat within 48 hours.
amatriciana.html.freezing: Freeze the cooled sauce separately for best texture, then defrost fully in the fridge and use within 24 hours. Cook fresh pasta when serving.
amatriciana.html.reheating: Add a splash of water and reheat once until steaming hot throughout, stirring well. Add freshly cooked pasta to thawed, reheated sauce.
amatriciana.html.substitutions: Pancetta can replace guanciale; Parmesan can replace Pecorino, with a milder result. Replace the wine with 50ml water if preferred.

creamy-tomato-sausage-gnocchi.html.storage: Cool promptly, refrigerate covered within 2 hours and eat within 48 hours.
creamy-tomato-sausage-gnocchi.html.freezing: For best texture, freeze the sausage and tomato sauce before adding cream, spinach and gnocchi. Defrost fully in the fridge and use within 24 hours; finish with fresh cream, spinach and freshly cooked gnocchi.
creamy-tomato-sausage-gnocchi.html.reheating: Reheat once until steaming hot throughout, stirring gently with a splash of water. Add freshly cooked gnocchi when reheating sauce-only portions.
creamy-tomato-sausage-gnocchi.html.substitutions: Use chicken sausages instead of pork, or kale instead of spinach, allowing longer for it to soften.

karahi.html.storage: Cool promptly and refrigerate covered within 2 hours. Use within 48 hours, or sooner if the base gravy has an earlier storage limit.
karahi.html.freezing: Freeze portions for later reheating only when made with freshly cooked chicken and freshly made gravy in this cooking session. Otherwise freeze the gravy separately before finishing the curry. Defrost fully in the fridge and use within 24 hours.
karahi.html.reheating: Reheat once until steaming hot throughout. If chilled chicken or gravy was already reheated when making this curry, do not reheat the finished curry again.
karahi.html.substitutions: For less heat, halve the fresh chilli and chilli powder. Black cardamom is omitted from this version. Use only chicken breast for the chicken version.
